newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS produces 144.8 mln tonnes sugar so far.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS produces 144.8 mln tonnes sugar so far.

text.p: Brazil's centre south region milled 144.8 million tonnes of sugar cane up to September 1, producing 6.52 million tonnes of sugar, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.

In a report made available to Reuters, the ministry's sugar and alcohol department said centre south cane production was 4.2 percent higher than the same period in the 1995/96 harvest and sugar production was up 6.4 percent.
The ministry also increased its forecast for sugar cane production in the north/northeast to 50 million tonnes from 48 million tonnes, due to "the good distribution of rain".

The report said the centre south region had produced about 7.54 million cubic metres of alcohol, an increase of 2.9 percent over 1995/96. Hydrous alcohol production represented 69.1 percent of the total and anhydrous 30.9 percent.
In the north/northeast, where the harvest is just beginning, it said it expected 3.207 million tonnes of sugar to be produced, 1.522 million tonnes of which would be exported.
Alcohol production was likely to reach 733,444 cubic metres of anhydrous and 1.223 million cubic metres of hydrous, the ministry said.

In the centre south, Sao Paulo state was responsible for 72 percent of total sugar cane milled, Parana for 9.8 percent, Minas Gerais for 4.6 percent, Mato Grosso for 4.1 percent and Goias for 3.7 percent.
The remaining 5.8 percent was distributed between Mato Grosso do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo and Rio Grande do Sul.
